props.title: Dead Set

sections.content: Dead Set (2008) brilliantly merges reality TV satire with zombie horror, setting its apocalyptic outbreak during a live season of Big Brother UK. Created by Charlie Brooker (before his Black Mirror (2011) fame), it viciously critiques celebrity culture while delivering genuine scares. The series shares DNA with 28 Days Later (2002), using similar fast-moving "infected" and capturing that same immediate, visceral terror of contemporary London under siege. The meta-commentary hits harder because it cast actual Big Brother presenters and used the real house location.

sections.content: The series particularly excels in its commentary on surveillance culture, predating but perfectly complementing films like The Cabin in the Woods (2011) and One Cut of the Dead (2017). The Big Brother house becomes both sanctuary and prison, with cameras continuing to roll even as civilization crumbles outside. This surveillance theme connects to later works like Host (2020), where our screen-mediated lives become the backdrop for horror.

Dead Set's influence can be seen in later meta-horror works like What We Do in the Shadows (2014) and Behind the Mask: The Rise of Leslie Vernon (2006), which similarly play with documentary/reality TV formats while delivering genuine genre thrills. The series also shares thematic DNA with Night of the Comet (1984), where pop culture and apocalypse collide in unexpected ways. SUBHEAD: Reality TV Horror Evolution

sections.content: Dead Set helped establish a subgenre that includes films like Series 7: The Contenders (2001) and My Little Eye (2002), where reality TV becomes a vehicle for horror storytelling. This trend continues in modern films like Spree (2020) and Dashcam (2021), where social media livestreaming creates new forms of horror. The series particularly resonates with V/H/S/99 (2022) and its reality TV segment that similarly skewers behind-the-scenes television production.
